segments.he:
טו.
עקר מעלות ההסתכלות וראית פני הצדיק, שזוכין על ידי זה לכל התקונים המבארים בפנים, הוא רק כשהוא באמת ובאמונה, שאז נקרא ראיה, כי כשרואה פני הצדיק ואינו מאמין בו, אין זה נקרא ראיה כלל, כי באמת אינו רואה את הצדיק כלל, מאחר שלפי דעתו אינו צדיק, כי אינו מאמין בו נמצא שאינו רואה את הצדיק כלל. (הלכות תפלין, הלכה ו, אות יב):
segments.en:
The essential virtue of gazing upon and beholding the face of the Tzadik — through which one merits all the repairs explained in the source text — is only when it is in truth and in faith. For only then is it called "seeing." For when one sees the face of the Tzadik but does not believe in him — this is not called seeing at all. For in truth he does not see the Tzadik at all, since according to his own understanding the Tzadik is not a Tzadik — as he does not believe in him. It is thus found that he does not see the Tzadik at all.

(Hilchos Tefillin, Halacha 6, item 12).

segments.he:
טז.
כל זמן שלא זכה האדם לידע מי הוא הצדיק האמת, שצריך להתקרב אליו ולהתדבק בו, אזי צריך להאמין ולהתדבק בכל הצדיקים, אף על פי שחולקין זה על זה. לא כמו הליצנים שאומרים, שמאחר שחולקים הצדיקים זה על זה - הוא שומע דברי שניהם וחולק על שניהם, כי זהו דברי ליצנות, ונוגעין בכפירות, רחמנא לצלן, רק האמת הוא להפך - שצריך להאמין בכולם, ולבלי להסתכל כלל על המחלקת שביניהם, מאחר שכולם מזהירים אותו לקים תורת משה, שבכתב ושבעל פה, כי רק מהאנשים מהאנשים הכופרים, ההולכים בדרכי החקירה, הרוצים להטות מתורת משה ללמד חכמות חיצוניות וכו', מהם צריכין להתרחק בתכלית הרחוק, אבל כל מי שמנהיג על פי על פי התורה, כפי שמסרו לנו רבותינו הקדושים בגמרא, ופוסקים וספרי יראים, המיוסדים על פי דבריהם הקדושים - בהם צריכים להתדבק, בכולם, כמו שכתוב: ובו תדבק ואמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה: 
הדבק בתלמידי חכמים. וזה בחינת יום טוב שני של גלויות, כי כמו שמחמירין מחמת ספק ועושין שני ימים טובים, כמו כן צריכין מחמת ספק להתקרב לכל הצדיקים, ההולכים על פי התורה, כי קדושת יום טוב היא בחינת קדושת הצדיק, כידוע. (הלכות תפלת המנחה, הלכה ו' אות יב):
segments.en:
As long as a person has not merited to know who is the true Tzadik — whom he must draw close to and cleave to — he must believe in and cleave to all Tzaddikim, even though they dispute one another. Not like the scoffers who say: since the Tzaddikim dispute one another, he listens to the words of both of them and disputes both of them — for this is words of mockery [leitzanus], touching upon heresy, G-d protect us. Rather, the truth is the opposite: one must believe in all of them, and not look at all at the disputes between them — since all of them admonish him to fulfill the Torah of Moshe, written and oral. For only from those people — [from those people] — the deniers who walk in the ways of philosophical investigation, who wish to turn away from the Torah of Moshe to teach external wisdoms, etc. — from them one must distance himself completely. But all who lead according to — [according to] — the Torah, as our holy sages transmitted to us in Gemara, and the Poskim, and the books of fear of G-d founded upon their holy words — to all of them one must cleave — to all of them — as it is written: "And to Him you shall cleave", and our Sages of blessed memory said: "Cleave to Torah scholars."

And this corresponds to yom tov shaini shel galuyos [the second day of Yom Tov in the diaspora]. For just as one is stringent on account of doubt and observes two days of Yom Tov — so too, on account of doubt, one must draw close to all Tzaddikim who walk according to the Torah. For the holiness of Yom Tov is the aspect of the holiness of the Tzadik, as is known.

(Hilchos Tefillas HaMinchah, Halacha 6, item 12).

history.en: It is a very severe prohibition to eat and drink before prayer — as explained in the holy Zohar. (Not as is common now, in our many sins, where people are lenient in this, especially regarding drinking coffee before prayer.) And many Tzaddikim were careful not to drink even water before prayer — even though it is technically permitted according to strict law. And through not eating before prayer — through this one draws the aspect of the repair drawn through a fast [ta'anis]. For this is also the aspect of a fast of hours [ta'anis sha'os]. And through this the speech is perfected — and one brings it out from the narrow passage of the throat. And one merits to speak complete words before G-d in his prayer. And through this the faith is completed — which is itself the aspect of prayer, as is known. Also through this one merits to begin each morning anew in the service of G-d — in the aspect of: "They are renewed each morning" [Lamentations 3:23].

segments.he:
יז.
העקר הוא אמונת חכמים, כי העקר הוא התכלית, וצריך כל אדם לחוס על עצמו ולחשב תמיד בכל יום על תכליתו הנצחי, ומה יהיה סופו וכו' ולזכות לתכלית הטוב באמת, אי אפשר כי אם על ידי אמונת חכמים כי אי אפשר להאדם להגיע ולחזר למקור נשמתו כי אם על ידי על ידי החכמים הצדיקים אמתיים, כי אפלו כשרים ויראים ועוסקים בתורה אינם יכולים להגיע לשלמותם כי אם על ידי החכמים והצדיקים אמתיים, מכל שכן מי שפגם איזה פגם, פגם, מכל שכן מי שפגם ועבר הרבה, חס ושלום, כמצוי עכשו בעוונותינו הרבים, בודאי אי אפשר לרפאתו בגוף ונפש כי אם על ידי הצדיקים הגדולים והנפלאים באמת, שיודעים לדרש את התורה בשלמות באמת, ויודעים שרשי נפשות של כל אחד מישראל בהתורה, ויודעים לפרש ולבאר כל הדרכים והעצות והנתיבות והתחבולות, שצריך כל אדם שבעולם, הרוצה לגשת אל הקדש, באפן שיוכל כל אחד לקבל רפואה לכל מיני חלי הנפש והגוף שבעולם. (הלכות שבת, הלכה ו', אות ג):
segments.en:
The essential thing is emunah b'chachamim [faith in the sages]. For the essential thing is the ultimate end [tachlis] — and every person must have consideration for himself and reflect always, each and every day, on his eternal ultimate purpose, and what will be his end, etc. And to merit the truly good ultimate purpose, it is impossible except through faith in the sages. For it is impossible for a person to reach and return to the source of his soul except through — [through] — the truly wise Tzaddikim. For even those who are upright and G-d-fearing and engage in Torah cannot reach their perfection except through the truly wise Tzaddikim. How much more so one who has incurred some blemish — [some blemish] — how much more so one who has transgressed and sinned greatly, G-d forbid, as is common now in our many sins — certainly he cannot be healed in body and soul except through the great and wondrous truly righteous ones, who know how to expound the Torah fully in truth, and know the root-sources of the souls of each person of Israel within the Torah, and know how to explain and clarify all the paths and counsels and trails and strategies that every person in the world requires — one who wishes to approach the holy — so that every person may receive healing for every manner of sickness of soul and body in the world.

(Hilchos Shabbos, Halacha 6, item 3).

history.en: Through sins, one causes, G-d forbid, the spirit of a person [ru'ach ho'odom] to become mingled with and exchanged for the spirit of an animal [ru'ach habeheimah]. This is the aspect of the exchange — that the prince's son was exchanged with the servant's son. And this is the secret of all the sacrifices [korbanos] — to extract the human spirit from the animal spirit. And each person — commensurate with how much he has mingled the human spirit with the animal spirit through his sins — when he does not merit to repair this during his lifetime, G-d forbid — then he must receive his punishment to be cast about within the hollow of a sling [kaf hakela] and to seek the sparks and the human spirit that he lost and cast into the animal spirit — until he receives his full punishment. And then he will be repaired. For the punishment is — [is] — for the sake of repair.

segments.he:
יח.
עקר כלל האמונה הקדושה הוא אמונת חכמים, כי הם ממשיכין לנו האמונה הקדושה בשלמות, כי בלא אמונת חכמים אמתיים גם אמונתו בהשם יתברך אינו בשלמות. (שם אות יא):
segments.en:
The essential foundation of all holy faith is emunah b'chachamim — faith in the sages. For they draw down for us the holy faith in its fullness. For without faith in the truly wise sages, even one's faith in G-d, blessed be He, is not complete.

(ibid., item 11).

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And through reciting the Torah portion of the sacrifices and the chapter Eizehu Mekoman, etc. — it is considered as if he offered sacrifices in those places. And through this he merits to extract the entire aspect of the human spirit from the animal spirit from all the places where they fell — [fell] — there. And to repair and elevate them from there. And this is the aspect of Pesukei d'Zimrah [the verses of song recited after this] — for the essential extraction of the human spirit from the animal spirit is through melody. Which is the aspect of the priests in their service and the Levites on their platform.

segments.he:
יט.
צריכים להודות ולהלל מאד להשם יתברך, כשזוכין לאמונת חכמים, כי על ידי זה נצולין ויוצאין מכל הצרות שבעולם, ברוחניות ובגשמיות וזה בחינת מודים דרבנן. (שם אות יט):
segments.en:
One must greatly give thanks and greatly praise G-d (blessed be He) when one merits faith in the sages — for through this one is saved and escapes from all the afflictions in the world, both in spirituality and in materiality. And this corresponds to Modim d'Rabbanan [the congregational acknowledgment during the Amidah].

(ibid., item 19).

history.en: The entire matter of the prince's son who was exchanged with the servant's son — explained in the story-tales — encompasses the entire Torah entirely. And all that has passed from the beginning of the sin of Adam the first — who was expelled from the Garden of Eden, etc. — until the end: when our righteous Mashiach will come and the kingship will return to the true prince's son. And all the essential service of a person in this world is only in this matter — as explained in the inner teachings. And this is what the secret of the morning blessings and the sacrifices and Pesukei d'Zimrah and the Kriyas Shma and the Shemoneh Esreh — and the Shemoneh Esreh — revolves around, as explained in the inner teachings.

segments.he:
כ.
צריך האדם לזהר, שלא לכנס לחקר במה שאין לו רשות בבחינת: במופלא ממך אל תדרש וכו', ותכף כשרואה מבוכה, שאי אפשר להשיגה ולהבינה - יברח משם, ויסמך רק על אמונה ומי שפוגם בזה, הוא בחינת פגם אכילת בשר בחלב. (הלכות דברים היוצאים מן החי, שבהלכות סימני בהמה וחיה טהורה, הלכה ד' אות מ):
segments.en:
A person must be careful not to enter into inquiry in areas where he has no permission — in the spirit of: "In what is too wondrous for you, do not seek, etc.". And the moment he perceives confusion — that it is impossible to grasp or understand it — he should flee from there, and rely only upon faith. And one who blemishes this is in the aspect of the blemish of eating meat in milk.

(Hilchos Devorim HaYotzim min HaChai (within Hilchos Simanai Beheimah v'Chayah Tehorah), Halacha 4, item 40).

history.en: The essential joy of Israel is through faith — in the aspect of: "I will rejoice in G-d" [Habakkuk 3:18]. And this is the aspect of the Kriyas Shma — which is the foundation of faith. And since joy is a complete stature [komah sheleimah] with 248 limbs — therefore, after Shema Yisroel one reads the three Torah portions, etc. — which contain 248 words in the Kriyas Shma, as our Sages of blessed memory said. And through joy one merits redemption — in the aspect of: "For in joy you shall go forth" [Isaiah 55:12]. And this is the aspect of the blessing of redemption [bircas ge'ulah] recited after the Kriyas Shma. And one must juxtapose the redemption to the prayer. For the essential perfection of the service of prayer is when it is in joy — in the aspect of: "Serve G-d in joy" [Psalms 100:2]. And prayer is the aspect of attachment [devekus] to G-d, as is known — and this is the ultimate purpose of joy: to rejoice in Him, blessed be He, and to cling to Him in wondrous and extraordinary attachment.

segments.he:
כא.
מי שלבו שלם עם השם, ואמונתו חזקה, ומאמין שהכל מתנהג רק ברצונו יתברך - אזי הוא בשמחה תמיד, ואין לו שום דאגה ופחד כלל משום דבר שבעולם. (הלכות כלי היין, הלכה א', אות א):
segments.en:
One whose heart is whole with G-d, and whose faith is strong, and who believes that everything is guided solely by the will of G-d (blessed be He) — he is in joy always, and has no worry or fear whatsoever about anything in the world.

(Hilchos K'lai HaYayin, Halacha 1, item 1).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And the essential construction of joy is through the ten types of melody. And therefore the essential prayer is with a quorum of ten [minyan]. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory said: "Any prayer that does not include among its worshipers [even] the sinners of Israel [is lacking], etc." [Kerisus 6b]. For this is the essential perfection of joy — to transform all kinds of sorrow and sighing into joy — so that they become a vehicle for holiness. And this is the aspect of the chelbenah [galbanum] in the incense [ketores]. For the incense is also the aspect of joy — in the aspect of: "incense gladdens the heart" [Proverbs 27:9]. And the chelbenah is the aspect of sorrow and sighing — which is also transformed into joy. And therefore every person must be careful to pray specifically with a congregation [tzibur] — so that even if he has some grip of sorrow and sighing — it too will be transformed into joy through the holiness of the large congregation. And therefore prayer is a healing for everything — for all healings come through joy.

segments.he:
כב.
הטבילה והטהרה במקוה, מסוגל לגדל ולהשלים את האמונה. (הלכות גלוח, הלכה ד', אות טז):
segments.en:
Immersion and purification in the mikveh is a segula [-propitious means] to grow and to complete one's faith.

(Hilchos Giluach, Halacha 4, item 16).

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: All the alien thoughts and all the confusions — all of them — are the aspects of: arlas lev [foreskin of the heart], cherpos lev [shame of the heart], sheviras lev [breaking of the heart] — for they shame and disgrace and break a person's heart. And this is the essential service of prayer — to purify and cleanse the heart from all evil loves and from all desires and confusions — which are the aspect of cherpos lev, arlas lev as above — through the speech of prayer. Which is the aspect of tzadik moshel [the Tzadik who rules] — which is the aspect of the holy point where the light of holy love dwells. And therefore at the time of prayer all the confusions and all the alien thoughts intensify — as is the way of those fighting one another: when one side comes to nullify the other — the other wishes to overpower against it. Therefore in truth at the time of prayer it is a great battle. And one must be very careful to bind the speech of prayer — which is the aspect of the point aforementioned — to the heart. In order to nullify the cherpos lev aforementioned.

segments.he:
כג.
אי אפשר לתקן בשלמות תאות ממון כל זמן שלא זכה לשלמות האמונה, וכן להפך אי אפשר לזכות לאמונה שלמה כל זמן שלא בטל תאות ממון, ואם כן מהיכן יתחיל על כן עקר העצה - רק לצעק להשם יתברך בכל עת, וזהו ההתחלה של כל ההתחלות, ואז יעזר לו השם יתברך, שיזכה לכל התקונים כאחד. (הלכות ערלה, הלכה ד', אות יח-יט):
segments.en:
It is impossible to completely repair the desire for money as long as one has not merited complete faith. And likewise the reverse: it is impossible to merit complete faith as long as the desire for money has not been nullified. And if so — from where does one begin? Therefore, the essential counsel is only to cry out to G-d (blessed be He) at all times. And this is the beginning of all beginnings. And then G-d (blessed be He) will help him, so that he merits all the repairs together.

(Hilchos Orlah, Halacha 4, items 18–19).

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: At the time of Minchah [the afternoon prayer] — then takfa d'dinah shalta [the force of strict judgment rules]. From which come all the obstacles from the service of G-d. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory warned especially not to delay the Minchah prayer — as is explained in the Mishnah: "A person should not sit before a barber, etc." Because the obstacles are most common then — since that is the time when most of the world is preoccupied with commerce and their livelihood. From which come all the obstacles from the service of G-d. And then a person must overpower himself more greatly with strong wills and great longings for G-d — in order to remember G-d within the commerce, within the intensity of the obstacles. And this is the essential [meaning]. And this is the aspect of the Minchah prayer. For prayer is the service of the heart — the aspect of ratzon [will]. But the essential intensification of the will is needed specifically at the time of Minchah. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory warned about it especially. For through the Minchah prayer one merits to draw the sweetening of the Minchah of Shabbos [minchah shel Shabbos] — when the essential illumination of the will — ra'ava d'ra'avin [the will of all wills] — shines, as is known. And because the holy will is the aspect of the minchas ani [offering of the poor] — therefore our Sages of blessed memory called this prayer by the name Minchah.

segments.he:
כד.
התורה והאמונה תלויים זה בזה, כי אי אפשר לקים את התורה כי אם על ידי אמונה, כמו שכתוב: כל מצותיך אמונה, וכן אין קיום להאמונה כי אם על ידי התורה. (הלכות דינים, הלכה ד', אות ז):
segments.en:
Torah and faith depend upon one another. For it is impossible to fulfill the Torah except through faith, as it is written: "All Your commandments are faith". And likewise there is no endurance to faith except through Torah.

(Hilchos Dinim, Halacha 4, item 7).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: All day a person is preoccupied with his affairs and commerce — which is the aspect of sleep [shenah]. The Minchah prayer is where he remembers G-d and awakens from his sleep — which is the aspect of the commerce. And he pauses to pray Minchah. And therefore the Minchah prayer is the aspect of Rosh Hashanah — which is the aspect of the awakening of the year [his'orrus hashanah]. For Yitzchak established the Minchah prayer — which is the aspect of Rosh Hashanah, the fear of Yitzchak [pachad Yitzchok]. And therefore at that time the judgment is loosened [dina sharya]. And since the essential nourishment of the outer forces comes from the aspect of judgments — therefore they decreed that one should not begin to eat or work [at that time] — so as not to forget to pray. And our Sages of blessed memory said: "A person must always be diligent in the Minchah prayer" — for then extra vigilance is needed for the reason mentioned above.

segments.he:
כה.
על ידי אמונת הרצון, דהינו שמאמין באמונה שלמה, שהכל מתנהג רק ברצונו יתברך, על ידי זה זוכה להארת הרצון, דהינו שיכסף וישתוקק להשם יתברך ולעבודתו יתברך ברצון חזק וכסופים גדולים, כמבאר בפנים. (הלכות ערב, הלכה ג', אות ג):
segments.en:
Through emunah b'ratzon [faith in the Divine will] — that is, believing with complete faith that everything is guided solely by the will of G-d (blessed be He) — through this one merits the illumination of ratzon [will]: that is, one yearns and longs for G-d (blessed be He) and for His service (blessed be He) with a strong will and great longings [kesuphim gedolim], as explained in the source text.

(Hilchos Erev, Halacha 3, item 3).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: The Minchah prayer with intention is a segula [-propitious means] for faith. And therefore Eliyahu merited to reveal the holy faith in the world at that time [minchah time].

segments.he:
כו.
על ידי שמצמצמין את המח לבלי להתגאות להיות חכם בעיניו, שירצה להשיג יותר משכלו, רק יצמצם מחו, וישפיל עצמו כאזוב וכתולעת, ויסמך עצמו על האמונה - על ידי זה דיקא זוכין לטהר תכלית החיצוניות ולקשר תכלית החיצוניות גם כן אל הפנימיות, שזה בחינת טהרת הפרה אדומה, כמבאר בפנים. (הלכות פקדון, הלכה ד' אות כג):
segments.en:
Through contracting the mind [moach] — so as not to be haughty or wise in one's own eyes, wishing to attain more than one's intellect can grasp — but rather to contract one's mind, and to humble oneself like hyssop [ezov] and like a worm, and to rely upon faith — through this, specifically, one merits to purify the ultimate externality and to connect the ultimate externality also to the innermost — which is the aspect of the purification of the parah adumah [red heifer], as explained in the source text.

(Hilchos Pikdonos, Halacha 4, item 23).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: Sometimes a person is in such smallness [katnus] that he cannot raise his voice at all. Even so, he must not despair of himself from prayer and supplication — and let him fulfill: "And you will be brought low from the earth you will speak… and from the dust your utterance will be chirped" [Isaiah 29:4]. Which is the aspect of: "From the depths I call You, G-d" [Psalms 130:1] — from depths of depths — the innermost of the heart — the aspect of: "Their heart cried out to G-d" [Lamentations 2:18]. Which is the aspect of the silent prayer [tefilah b'lochash] — which our Sages of blessed memory ordained for the smallest of the small. And also for the greatest of the great. For the very smallest — all their prayer is in the aspect of silent prayer as above. And their entire repair is through the great Tzaddikim — who also pray in a whisper [b'lochash]. For they ascend in their prayer to the aspect of Atikah [the Ancient One] — where the aspect of the whisper resides. The aspect of: "wise of hidden things and understanding of the whisper" [Isaiah 3:3]. For there is the aspect of: "a fence for wisdom is silence." And this is the aspect of: "Why do you cry out to Me?" [Exodus 14:15] — at Atikah the matter depends, as is explained in the holy Zohar. That is, for there at Atikah there is no crying out — only silence and a whisper. And this is the aspect of: "G-d will fight for you and you shall be silent" [Exodus 14:14]. For there in the time of katnus — one must cry out to G-d greatly. But in any case — for one must also strengthen himself even then in prayer and supplication — to pray in a whisper at least, from the depths of the heart — as mentioned above. And afterwards one merits to pray with a loud voice. Which is the aspect of the silent prayer — and afterwards the prayer leader [shali'ach tzibur] prays aloud.

segments.he:
כז.
על ידי אמונת חכמים בשלמות, על ידי זה נשמר העולם עם כל עשירויותיהם וחפציהם מכל מיני הזקות וחסרונות. גם צריכין לזה שיהיה אהבה ושלום גדול בין ישראל. (שם הלכה ה', אות ב):
segments.en:
Through complete faith in the sages — through this the world is preserved, together with all its riches and possessions, from all manner of damages and deficiencies. And for this there must also be great love and great peace among Israel.

(ibid., Halacha 5, item 2).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: Yaakov our Father, peace be upon him, through the greatness of his holiness, merited to lower himself to the very depth of the falls of all of Israel — in the general and the particular — and of every generation until the very footsteps of the Mashiach. And therefore he established the evening prayer [arvis] — which is at the time of complete darkness. For he illuminates the heart of Israel: that even in the utmost complete darkness one must also strengthen himself to engage in prayer. For lais re'usa tava d'is'avad [no good intention is ever lost]. And this he established at the time he merited to encounter the place — which is the place of the Temple. And there he merited to fully attain the very essence of the virtue of the awakening from below [is'arusa d'lisata]: that even any small awakening whatsoever — from whatever aspect and level it is — is never lost forever. For the true Tzadik — in the aspect of Yaakov — watches over this and gathers and collects everything and builds from it wondrous edifices. As all of this is explained in the inner teachings. And therefore he established the evening prayer — that even in the darkness of the night and actual gloom a person should awaken to pray and cry out to Him, blessed be He — in the aspect of: "From the belly of She'ol I cried out" [Jonah 2:3]. For even a cry from the lowest depths is never lost forever.

segments.he:
כח.
עקר עבדות ויגיעת הפרנסה נמשך מבחינת פגם אמונת חכמים, כי על ידי פגם אמונת חכמים נופל לעבדות, ופרנסתו בדחק גדול כל כך, עד שמוכרח להשכיר עצמו לעבד אצל חברו בשביל פרנסה אבל על ידי אמונת חכמים זוכה לחרות לבטל מעצמו על עבדות ויגיעת הפרנסה, ופרנסתו נמשכת לו ברוח ובשפי גדול. (שם, אות כו כז):
segments.en:
The essential subjugation [avdus] and toil of earning a livelihood derives from the aspect of the blemish of faith in the sages. For through the blemish of faith in the sages one falls into subjugation — and his livelihood comes with such great strain that he is forced to hire himself out as a servant to his fellow for the sake of sustenance. But through faith in the sages one merits freedom — to nullify from oneself the subjugation and the toil of earning a livelihood — and his livelihood flows to him with ease and great abundance.

(ibid., items 26–27).

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: In truth — all that G-d does with a person is all for his benefit. As our Sages of blessed memory said: a person must say: "All that is done from Heaven — is done for good" [Berochois 60b]. If so, seemingly it is difficult: why did G-d command us to pray regarding the affliction, G-d protect us? For all the sufferings and afflictions, G-d forbid, are truly great goodnesses — to cause him to merit through them the life of eternity. But in truth — certainly all that G-d does with a person is all for the good. And even so, a person must pray and beseech G-d to emerge from the affliction to spaciousness. For the essential creation of the world was for the sake of the human being who has free will — that everything be delivered into the hands of the person. That is, the person specifically should make vessels and channels to draw down His bounty and kindness, blessed be He, below. And without the repair of the vessels — made by the person — the flow of kindness cannot descend below. For if the kindness were to descend before the repair of the vessels — it would be in the aspect of: "an abundance of oil causes the lamp to be extinguished." And then the kindness would be transformed into severe judgment, G-d forbid.

segments.he:
כט.
עקר שלמות אמונת חכמים הוא, כשמפוזר ממונו להחזיק את התלמיד חכם ולהתקרב אליו. (שם, אות כו'):
segments.en:
The essential perfection of faith in the sages is when one's money is spread out to support the Torah scholar and to draw close to him.

(ibid., item 26).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And the essential repair of the vessels is through Torah and prayer. And primarily through prayer. And therefore before a person prays — certainly everything that comes upon him is a great goodness, even sufferings, G-d forbid. For everything is for his benefit. For according to his deeds — no flow and vitality can descend to him except through this. And even this comes in great kindness. For if only kindness without any judgment at all were to flow to him — it would be, G-d forbid, in the aspect of an abundance of light that damages more. Therefore the essential repair is through prayer. For through prayer one sweetens the judgments and repairs vessels — in a manner that one can receive the flow of His blessed kindness without sufferings. Only through the repairs of the vessels that he repaired through prayer. And therefore the essential repair of prayer is through gazing at the purpose [tachlis] and including all the prayer in the One — where it is entirely good. As explained in the inner teachings. For without this — one cannot pray at all because of the aforementioned difficulty. As our Sages of blessed memory posed: "But does one give a child whatever he wants?" For since G-d knows the truth — that these sufferings from deficiency of livelihood and the like are for his eternal benefit — how will G-d hear his prayer to give him what he asks and thereby cause him eternal harm, G-d forbid? As in what is written: "There is wealth kept for its owner to his detriment" [Ecclesiastes 5:12]. And as is brought in the holy Zohar: "they prayed for wealth in this world — and afterwards it killed them", G-d forbid.

segments.he:
ל.
בכל מה שעובר על האדם הן בפרנסה, הן בעבודת השם, ונדמה לו, שאי אפשר לעבד את השם מחמת דחקות הפרנסה ורבוי הבלבולים והרעיונים העוברים עליו - ידע, שכל זה נמשך מפגם אמונת חכמים, ויזכר עצמו בכל פעם על ידי זה לשוב בתשובה שלמה על פגם אמונת חכמים, ויאמין מעתה באמת בכל ספרי הצדיקים והחכמים אמתיים, עד שיזכה על ידי זה לינק מהשכל הכולל, שעל ידי זה נמתק ונתתקן הכל. (שם, אות לב):
segments.en:
In everything that passes over a person — whether in livelihood, or in the service of G-d — and it appears to him that it is impossible to serve G-d on account of the strain of livelihood and the multitude of confusions and thoughts that befall him — let him know that all of this derives from the blemish of faith in the sages. And let him remind himself each time through this to return in complete teshuvah for the blemish of faith in the sages — and from now on let him truly believe in all the books of the truly righteous and truly wise sages, until he merits through this to draw nourishment from the encompassing intellect [seichel hakolel] — through which everything is sweetened and repaired.

(ibid., item 32).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And therefore in truth the essential repair of prayer is through gazing at the true purpose in truth — and knowing and believing that everything is for the good. And then specifically one can pray afterwards for all that he needs. For then he can draw repairs from the light of the impression of the nullification toward the purpose — through which vessels will be made to draw through them His blessed abundant bounty and kindness in perfection with no lack of anything: livelihood and wealth and health — and health — children, life, and sustenance [banei, chayai, mezonai]. And even so — no harm and loss whatsoever will come to him through this, G-d forbid, in any direction — neither in this world nor in the World to Come. Rather, everything will be for eternal good as well. Since he has already repaired the vessels properly to receive through them the flow of kindness.

segments.he:
לא.
הפלת נפלים בא, חס ושלום, על ידי פגם אמונת חכמים. (שם, אות לה):
segments.en:
Miscarriages come, G-d forbid, through the blemish of faith in the sages.

(ibid., item 35).

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And therefore in truth no person knows how to pray in perfection — except the truly righteous Tzaddikim. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "One who has a sick person in his house — let him go to a sage and ask him to pray for mercy." And other people must bind their prayer to the Tzaddikim aforementioned — and they will elevate their prayer as is proper — to draw for them the flow of what they need: children, life, and sustenance, etc. In a manner that it will not harm them eternally, G-d forbid. Rather, on the contrary — through the flow specifically they will be repaired and return to G-d.

segments.he:
לב.
מענין הרוח סערה וענן גדול ואש מתלקחת, המסעיר ומחשיך ובוער עתה בעולם מאד על ידי כתות האפיקורסים, המתגברים בכל יום, ומי יודע מה ילד יום, רחמנא לצלן, אך כבר הקדים לנו השם יתברך רפואה למכה על ידי גדולי הצדיקים האמתיים וכו'. (הלכות נזיקין, הלכה ד', אות כח, ל):
segments.en:
Regarding the matter of the raging wind, and great cloud, and consuming fire — which now storms and darkens and blazes very greatly in the world through the sects of the apikorsim [heretics], who grow stronger each and every day, and who knows what the day will yet bring forth, G-d protect us — but G-d (blessed be He) has already provided the healing before the wound for us, through the great truly righteous Tzaddikim, etc.

(Hilchos Nezikkin, Halacha 4, items 28, 30).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And therefore in truth there are many wonders and hidden matters in this matter of prayer. And therefore in truth it is forbidden to be stubborn and to press oneself about anything in one's prayer — as is explained elsewhere. For perhaps in truth it is impossible to fulfill one's request even through prayer — as it may harm him more, G-d forbid, if his request is fulfilled. And if he presses and is very stubborn in his prayer — it could be that he will accomplish with G-d the fulfillment of his request. For a person has great power to accomplish through his prayer. But it will not be for his benefit, G-d forbid. For he has not yet merited through his prayer to repair the vessel in perfection that is needed for receiving the flow that he wants. It is thus found: that as long as he is not praying for his needs — all the lacks he has are a great goodness for him. But through prayer he repairs vessels properly — through which he can — [can] — receive the flow of kindness to fill all the lacks — and it will not — [not] — harm him at all eternally either. And all of this — through gazing in truth at the purpose — which is entirely good as above.

segments.he:
~לג. 
עקר תקון הברית בשלמות הוא על ידי אמונת חכמים. (הלכות פריה ורביה, הלכה א', אות י):
segments.en:
The essential complete repair of the bris [covenant] is through faith in the sages.

(Hilchos Priyah u'Riviyah, Halacha 1, item 10).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And therefore in truth the essential prayer must truly be for one's eternal purpose. And this is the aspect of what is brought in the sacred books: that the essential prayer must be for the sake of completing the lack of the Shechinah, as it were. And therefore even the prayer one prays for one's physical needs — one should pray that G-d give him all his needs in a manner that will bring him eternal success. And this is the aspect of the order of the Shemoneh Esreh [Amidah] that our Sages of blessed memory arranged for us. And we begin first with the praise of the Omnipresent — in the first three blessings. And in the first blessing we mention how He, blessed be He, bestows good kindnesses — and all that He does is entirely for the good. And He is the King, helper, savior, and shield. And afterwards in the blessing of mechayeh hamaisim [Who revives the dead] — one includes also all other salvations and sustenance and healing. And one includes them many times together with the matter of the revival of the dead. That is, we praise and give thanks to G-d that all that He does with us is for our eternal benefit — which is the aspect of the revival of the dead. And only for this does He cause wondrous salvations to sprout for us at all times also in the physical: in matters of sustenance and healing and the like. All in a manner that will bring eternal success — also after the Revival. And thus it is understood that also what sometimes delays the flow, G-d forbid — all of it is for our eternal benefit after the Revival. For since G-d is so good and so beneficent and so all-powerful — and does kindness with the entire world at all times — sustains the living, etc. — if so, from where does it come that sometimes the flow is delayed? Certainly one must believe that it is only for eternal benefit. And therefore there the blessing mentions the matter of the Revival of the Dead many times in close proximity to the matter of sustenance. For in the matter of sustenance, a person's heart is most vexed — and it is hardest for him every time on account of the delay in livelihood. And therefore one must especially be reminded in this matter — that all the sustenance and provision that G-d provides for a person — all of it is for his eternal benefit after the Revival of the Dead. And for this very same reason the sustenance is sometimes delayed — for his eternal benefit afterwards.

segments.he: ערך אכילה
segments.en: Eating

origin.notice: Editorial English rendering of the supplied Hebrew heading or closing text.

requiredNotes.text: This field is a heading or inscription, not a prose passage.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And afterwards one says Kedushah and the blessing Atah Kadosh [You are holy] — which is the aspect of the very essence of the purpose: that all of Israel should merit after the Revival to sanctify His Name together with all the holy ones who will praise Him forever. And after having arranged the praise of the Omnipresent and proclaimed that all that G-d does is entirely for the good — then one prays for his needs. And even this one begins with the most essential: for knowledge and repentance and forgiveness of sin. And then one prays for the needs of the body. But all our intention even in this is only for the eternal purpose. For we know and acknowledge that G-d is all-powerful — and all that He does with us is entirely for the good. Only even so it is His blessed will that we pray before Him for our needs — in order to make vessels to receive the flow in perfection. And the essential thing — only for the sake of the eternal purpose. And therefore we recite the Kriyas Shma before the prayer. For through the Kriyas Shma we are encompassed in the One. And then specifically one can pray — as mentioned above.

segments.he:
א.
על ידי שמפרישין חלה זוכין שיהיה הלחם והמזון בבחינת מזונא דנשמתא, בבחינת אכילת הצדיקים, בחינת: 
צדיק אוכל לשבע נפשו. (הלכות ציצית, הלכה ה', אות כט):
segments.en:
Through separating challah [the portion of dough set aside for the kohen] one merits that the bread and the food should be in the aspect of mazonah d'nishmasa — nourishment of the soul — in the aspect of the eating of the Tzaddikim, the aspect of: "A Tzadik eats to the satisfaction of his soul".

(Hilchos Tzitzis, Halacha 5, item 29).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: One must strengthen oneself greatly in complete faith — to believe in himself that he has the power to accomplish anything through his prayer. For there are many types of weakness of mind in a person's heart in this matter — as every person knows within himself. And the majority of people imagine that they have no power for this. And therefore they do not strengthen themselves in prayer. And therefore one must toil with very great toil and service to strengthen himself to pray with intention. And the essential toil is at the beginning — that is, at the time he begins to strengthen himself to pray with intention — in the aspect of: "all beginnings are difficult." For at that time he has not yet seen any action from his prayer. But when he merits to overpower himself with all his strength to pray with intention — until he merits to accomplish some thing through his prayer — such as he prayed about some matter and was answered — then he is strengthened in this to believe even in himself that he has the power to accomplish through his prayer. Since he sees that G-d has already heard his prayer too and he was answered. And then a complete vessel is formed for him to receive the flow through the words of prayer. For the essential formation of the vessel is through faith — that is, through believing even in himself that G-d hears his prayer.

segments.he:
ב.
יש צדיקים אמתיים, שהם קדושים באמת, ושברו תאות אכילה לגמרי, עד שאינם יכולים לאכל כי אם מעט דמעט, וגם זה המעט שאוכלין הוא בקדושה נוראה, עד שכל מאכלם ומזונם אינו מאכל ומזון שהעולם נזונים ממנו, כי מאכלם הוא בחינת מן, שהוא לחם אבירים, מאכל מלאכים. ויכול האדם לזכות, שיהיה כל מאכלו וסעודתו בבחינת לחם הפנים, ויש צדיקים שזכו, שכל מאכלם אינו רק מהתנוצצות האותיות הקדושות, שבאותו הדבר שאוכל ושותה, נמצא, שצדיקים כאלו אינם אוכלים ושותים מאכל ומשקה של שאר בני אדם כלל, רק אוכלין ושותין אותיות קדושות וכו', אך צריכין לשמר את עצמו מאד, כי יש צבועים ושקרנים, המתדמין עצמן כקוף בפני אדם, ומרגילין עצמן לאכל מעט מחמת גדלות וגסות הרוח כדי להתכבד ולהתיקר על ידי זה, מחמת שרואין, שזה הדבר חשוב עכשו וסוברין, שבשביל זה יקבלו אותם לרבי ומנהיג, אף על פי שלא התחילו עדין לשבר שום תאוה ומדה כלל, וגם תאות אכילה לא התחילו לשבר כלל, רק ממעטים באכילה בשביל כבוד כנ"ל. (הלכות תפלה, הלכה ד', אות ו):
segments.en:
There are truly righteous Tzaddikim who are holy in truth and who have broken the desire for eating completely — to the point that they cannot eat except the very slightest amount, and even this small amount that they eat is in awesome holiness — to the point that all their food and nourishment is not the food and nourishment upon which the [rest of the] world is sustained. For their food is in the aspect of the mon [manna] — which is lechem abirim, the bread of mighty ones, the food of the angels. And a person can merit that all his food and his meal should be in the aspect of the lechem hapanim [the showbread in the Temple]. And there are Tzaddikim who have merited that all their food is only from the sparkling of the holy letters [osiyos kedoshos] that are within the thing he eats and drinks — it is thus found that such Tzaddikim do not eat and drink the food and drink of other human beings at all; rather they eat and drink holy letters, etc.

But one must guard oneself very much — for there are hypocrites and liars who make themselves resemble [another, like] a monkey before a human being. And they accustom themselves to eat little on account of pride and arrogance of spirit, in order to be honored and esteemed through this — because they see that this matter is considered important nowadays, and they think that on account of this they will be accepted as a rebbe and leader. Even though they have not yet begun to break any desire or character trait whatsoever, and have not even begun to break the desire for eating at all — they merely eat little for the sake of honor, as above.

(Hilchos Tefilah, Halacha 4, item 6).

history.en: There are two kinds of kelipos [husks] that confuse a person's mind from strengthening himself in prayer. They are the husks of Eisav and Yishmo'el — which are the husks of the orlah [foreskin] and the peri'ah [secondary membrane]. The husk of Eisav-Amalek is the aspect of the outright orlah — for he denies the very foundation and does not acknowledge prayer at all. And he misleads a person's heart to say that prayer accomplishes nothing, G-d forbid — since the exile drags on for so long and every day one cries out and is not saved. And through the commandment of circumcision [bris milah] — which cuts the orlah that covers the bris — through this his evil husk is nullified and the aspect of the repair of the bris is drawn. Through which one merits to always strengthen himself in prayer. For the essential repair of prayer is through the repair of the bris.

segments.he:
ג.
מי שמזלזל, חס ושלום בנטילת ידים ואוכל בלי נטילה, הוא בחינת פגם אכילת עץ הדעת, שכולל כל העוונות שבתורה, ומשם עקר אחיזת סטרא דמסאבא, זוהמות הנחש, ועל כן אמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה, שחיב מיתה בחינת: כי ביום אכלך ממנו וגו', ועל ידי נטילת ידים ממשיך עליו הטהרה מבחינת: ונהר יוצא מעדן, שהוא בחינת הים החכמה, ואז אכילתו בבחינת: מכל עץ הגן אכל תאכל, בחינת אכילה דקדושה, בחינת מן, שמאיר בו הארת הרצון כנ"ל. (הלכות נטילת ידים לסעודה, הלכה ג', אות ג,ה):
segments.en:
One who is careless, G-d forbid, about the washing of hands [netilas yodayim] and eats without washing — this is in the aspect of the blemish of eating from the Tree of Knowledge, which encompasses all the sins in the Torah. And from there is the primary hold of the sitra d'mesava [the impure side], the defilement of the serpent. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory said that he is liable to death — in the aspect of: "For on the day you eat from it, etc.".

But through washing the hands one draws upon himself purity from the aspect of: "And a river goes out from Eden" — which is the aspect of the sea of wisdom [yam hachochmah]. And then his eating is in the aspect of: "From every tree of the garden you may surely eat" — the aspect of eating in holiness, the aspect of the mon, in which the illumination of the ratzon [Divine will] shines, as above.

(Hilchos Netilas Yodayim L'seudah, Halacha 3, items 3, 5).

history.en: But there is still another husk — the husk of the skin of peri'ah — which is the aspect of the husk of Yishmo'el. From which a different error is drawn in a person's heart — to become lax in prayer, G-d forbid. Because it seems to him that G-d has certainly already heard his prayer. Especially when he sees some sprouting of a ray of salvation — then it seems to him that his prayer has already been received. And he becomes lax about praying further. And this is drawn from the aspect of the husk of Yishmo'el — who is named thus from: "For G-d has heard your affliction" [Genesis 16:11] — and its Targum: "for G-d has received your prayer."

segments.he:
ד.
על ידי התפלה, על ידי זה מחזק ומתקן את נפשו ומזכך הדמים שלו, שבהם מלובש הנפש, ויכול אחר כך לאכל ולתקן הנפשות המלובשים במאכל, מה שאין כן קדם התפלה, ועל כן אסור לאכל קדם התפלה. (הלכות סעודה, הלכה א'):
segments.en:
Through prayer, one thereby strengthens and repairs his soul and purifies his blood — within which the soul is clothed — and he can afterwards eat and thereby repair the souls that are clothed within the food. This is not the case before prayer. And therefore it is forbidden to eat before prayer.

(Hilchos Seudah, Halacha 1).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: But in truth — even when one has not yet seen any salvation — one must believe that no prayer is in vain, G-d forbid. And to strengthen oneself in prayer even more. And likewise the reverse — even when one sees some salvation — it is forbidden to nullify and become lax in one's prayer because of this. Rather, one must rejoice in the salvation and give thanks for the past — and cry out for the future. For we still need many, very many salvations all the days of our lives — until we merit to come to what we need to come to — for which purpose we came into this world. And if one becomes lax in prayer because it seems to him that he has already accomplished much through his prayer — which is drawn from the aspect of the husk of Yishmo'el, the husk of peri'ah — through this, G-d forbid, the completion of his salvation is delayed and his exile is prolonged, G-d forbid. And then the husk of Eisav-Amalek — which is the husk of orlah — returns and arouses — and darkens his heart entirely from strengthening himself in his prayer through this very thing: that he sees that he has been crying out for so long and still is not answered with complete salvation.

segments.he:
ה.
עקר תקון האכילה בקדושה הוא על ידי צדקה, ועל כן צריכין להפריש לצדקה קדם האכילה ולהזמין לעני על שולחנו, כמבאר בספרים הקדושים, וזה מחמת שעל ידי צדקה נעשה כלי לקבל השפעת נעם העליון, שזה עקר תקון האכילה - לקשר הטעם ונעימת המאכל והמשקה לשרשו, לבחינת נעם העליון כנ"ל. (הלכות ברכת הפרות, הלכה ד' אות ט):
segments.en:
The essential repair of eating in holiness is through tzedakah [charity]. And therefore one must set aside for tzedakah before eating, and to invite a poor person to one's table — as is explained in the holy books. And this is because through tzedakah one becomes a vessel [keli] to receive the flow of the supernal delight [no'am ha'elyon] — which is the essential repair of eating: to bind the taste and pleasantness of the food and drink to its root, to the aspect of the supernal delight, as above.

(Hilchos Bircas HaPeiros, Halacha 4, item 9).

history.en: And this is the aspect of: "one who was circumcised but did not perform peri'ah — it is as if he was not circumcised." And this is the aspect of: "And Mordechai returned" [Esther 6:12] — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: he returned to his sackcloth and his fast [Megillah 16a]. For even though he had already seen such a wondrous salvation — that they had made him ride upon the king's horse and proclaimed before him, etc. — even so, he did not become lax through this in his prayer and his crying out. And likewise regarding Esther it is written: "And Esther spoke further before the king, etc. — and she wept and implored him to remove the evil of Haman, etc." [Esther 8:3]. And this alludes to all of Kneses Yisroel [the Congregation of Israel] — who are the aspect of Esther. That even when they see great salvations and wondrous miracles — that the sitra achra in the aspect of Haman-Amalek has already fallen greatly, and they have hung him and his sons — [and his sons] — on the tree — even so they are not satisfied with this and still stand and pray and weep and implore before Him, blessed be He — like a child who wheedles before his father — to remove the evil of Haman who is the sitra achra entirely. So that they merit to be purified and sanctified entirely.

segments.he:
ו.
כל מיני טרפות נמשכין מבחינת פגם הברית, ועל כן יש שבעים טרפות כנגד הרע הכולל של שבעים לשון, שכולם משוקעים בתאוה זו מאד, ועל ידי אכילה בכשרות, דהינו שנשמרין בשלמות מנבלות וטרפות וכו', על ידי זה נכנע הכסילות, וזוכין לתקון הדעת ולתקון הברית ולפרנסה ברוח. (הלכות טרפות, הלכה א', אות א-ב):
segments.en:
All manner of treifos [animals with halachically disqualifying injuries or defects] derive from the aspect of the blemish of the bris. And therefore there are seventy categories of treifah — corresponding to the encompassing evil of the seventy languages, all of whom are deeply sunk in this desire. And through eating b'kashrus [in ritual fitness] — that is, being perfectly guarded from nevailos [animals that died without valid ritual slaughter] and treifos, etc. — through this, foolishness [kesiluth] is subdued, and one merits the repair of da'as [knowledge/awareness] and the repair of the bris, and livelihood with ease.

(Hilchos Treifos, Halacha 1, items 1–2).

requiredNotes.text: שבעים לשון is rendered literally as seventy languages, rather than nations. The claim about seventy categories is the source’s own assertion, not an independently established count.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: For even though certainly one must give much thanks for the salvations that have already been done for him — even so, we still need to greatly multiply prayer. For we still need many salvations all the days of our lives. Therefore one must strengthen oneself to always greatly multiply prayer.

segments.he:
ז.
עקר הברורים ביותר הוא באכילת בשר, שהוא מיני החי, שיש בהם חיות ונפשות, ועל כן בודאי אי אפשר לאכל בשר כראוי כי אם על ידי התקשרות לצדיקים, אשר על ידם יש לנו כח לברר. ועל כן אמרו אמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה: עם הארץ אסור לאכל בשר, כי עם הארץ הוא אפלו קרא ושנה ולא שמש תלמידי חכמים, כמו שאמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה, הינו מי שאינו מקושר לצדיקים וחכמים אמתיים, בודאי אי אפשר לו לאכל בשר, מאחר שאין לו כח לברר הנפשות והניצוצות הקדושים שיש בבשר כנ"ל. (הלכות סימני עוף טהור, הלכה ב', אות ג):
segments.en:
The essential act of birurim [extraction of the holy sparks] occurs most of all in the eating of meat — which is of the animal kingdom, within which there are vitality and souls. Therefore certainly it is impossible to eat meat properly except through attachment [hiskasherus] to Tzaddikim, through whom we have the power to extract [levorar].

And therefore our Sages of blessed memory said — [said]: "An am ho'oretz [unlearned person, one unattached to Torah sages] is forbidden to eat meat." For an am ho'oretz — as our Sages of blessed memory said — is even one who has read Torah and studied Mishnah but has not attended upon Torah scholars [shimesh talmidei chachamim]. That is: one who is not attached to the truly righteous and wise — certainly it is impossible for him to eat meat, since he has no power to extract the souls and holy sparks [nitzotzos] that are within the meat, as above.

(Hilchos Simanai Oif Tahor, Halacha 2, item 3).

history.en: Tefillin are written on the skin of an animal [ohr beheimah] — this is the aspect of people who are as learned as a person [adom] yet make themselves like an animal [beheimah]. That is, one must make himself like an animal — to set aside one's mind entirely, as if one has no mind at all — and rely only on faith. And then through this one's mind is clarified and the crookedness [akmimusin] in one's heart is straightened. For when a person sees that he has crookedness in his heart — especially when he has, G-d forbid, much crookedness in his heart — then he must set aside his mind entirely as if he has no mind at all — and go only in wholeness [temimus] and simplicity [peshitus] alone. And then he merits afterwards to great knowledge [da'as] and to straighten out the crookedness in his heart. And all of this is the aspect of tefillin.

segments.he:
ח.
על ידי שאין האדם נזהר ממאכלי עכו"ם ומיין שנגע בו עכו"ם, על ידי זה נדבק בו רע הכולל, ויכול לבוא על ידי זה לפגם הברית מאד, חס ושלום: ועל ידי שנזהר ממאכלם ויינם, על ידי זה זוכה לתקון הברית ושיתגלו לו סודות התורה. (הלכות מאכלי עכו"ם), הלכה א', אות ג):
segments.en:
Through one's not being careful about the foods of gentiles [akum] and wine that a gentile has touched — through this the encompassing evil clings to him, and he can come through this to a very serious blemish of the bris, G-d forbid. And through being careful about their food and their wine — through this he merits the repair of the bris and the revelation of Torah secrets.

(Hilchos Ma'achalei Akum, Halacha 1, item 3).

history.en: Our Sages of blessed memory said: "Every single day a person's yetzer hara overpowers him — and were it not for the Holy One, blessed be He, helping him — he could not prevail against it" [Kiddushin 30b]. "Every single day the yetzer hara overpowers him" — this derives from the aspect of: "At first the thought arose to create the world with the attribute of strict judgment [midas hadin]". For this judgment arouses itself every single day — and wishes, G-d forbid, to conduct the world in this aspect. And from there the yetzer hara is aroused and intensifies — drawing from there every single day. For the essential yetzer hara and sitra achra derives from the aspect of judgments — drawn from the beginning of the contraction of the vacated space [chalal hapanui]. But G-d immediately has compassion and precedes the attribute of mercy before the attribute of judgment — as our Sages of blessed memory said: "He saw that the world could not endure [through judgment alone], etc." Which is the aspect of the help and assistance He provides the person every single day to shatter the yetzer hara — which is from the attribute of judgment. And this is the aspect of the tefillin of Rashi — where the kindnesses [chassadim] precede the strengths [gevuros]. And this is the aspect of: "He preceded the attribute of mercy and paired it with the attribute of judgment" — which is the essential governance and sustaining of the entire world. And therefore the essential tefillin that everyone wears are those of Rashi — for this is the essential governance and sustaining of the world through this aspect.

segments.he:
ט.
אין ראוי לשתות יין ומשקה המשכר כי אם מעט להרחיב דעתו, וגם זה בשבת ויום טוב וסעודת מצוה דיקא, וגם זה רק כשזוכה להתקשר לצדיקי אמת, שכבר זכו לקדושת הברית בתכלית השלמות, ועל ידם יכול כל אחד להמשיך על עצמו קדושת הברית, שהוא בחינת קדושת השבת, בחינת שבעים פנים, בחינת שבעים נפש לבית יעקב, ואז דיקא יכול לשתות מעט יין בשבת ויום טוב לשמח נפשו להרחיב דעתו, כדי שיוכל להתעורר להרגיש ביותר מתיקת נעימת עריבת קדושת התורה, קדושת ישראל, קדושת שבת, שנמשך עלינו בכח הצדיקי אמת, כמבאר בפנים. וגם אז צריכין לזהר מאד לשתות במדה במדה ובמשקל, לזכות שיהיה בבחינת יין המשמח, לזכות על ידי השמחה דקדושה להתדבק בהשם יתברך ובתורה ובצדיקים ולהרגיש ביותר גדולת השם יתברך והתורה והצדיקים, כל חד כפום מה דמשער בלבה. אבל אלו הקובעים עצמם על היין גם בימי החל, ולא די להם בכל זה, כי אם שבאים על ידי זה לליצנות ומחלקת, וחולקין על הצדיקים אמתיים, ואפלו אנשים הכשרים קצת, שאינם מתעוררים על ידי שתית היין לליצנות גמור, רק ששוגה בו, שעל ידי השתיה הוא שוגה וטועה עצמו, עד שמהפך האמת ודובר סרה על יראי השם האמתיים, כי נדמה לו, שנטו מן האמת, חס ושלום, וכל הטעות הזה בא לו על ידי רבוי שתית היין - על זה נאמר: כל שוגה בו לא יחכם, ופגמם וקלקולם על ידי זה מרובה מאד, כמבאר בפנים. (הלכות יין נסך, הלכה ד', אות ד ז):
segments.en:
It is not fitting to drink wine and intoxicating beverages except in small measure to broaden the mind [l'harchiv da'as] — and even this, specifically on Shabbos and Yom Tov and at a seudas mitzvah [a meal in honor of a commandment]. And even this only when one has merited to be attached to the truly righteous Tzaddikim who have already merited the holiness of the bris to the ultimate degree of perfection — and through them every person can draw upon himself the holiness of the bris, which is the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos, the aspect of the seventy faces [shivim panim], the aspect of the seventy souls of the house of Yaakov. And then, specifically, one can drink a little wine on Shabbos and Yom Tov to gladden his soul and broaden his mind — so that he can awaken himself to feel more deeply the sweetness and the pleasantness and the agreeableness of the holiness of Torah, the holiness of Israel, the holiness of Shabbos, which is drawn upon us through the power of the truly righteous Tzaddikim, as explained in the source text.

And even then one must be extremely careful to drink in measure — [in measure] — and in proper weight, to merit that it be in the aspect of the wine that gladdens [yayin hamesamaich], to merit through the joy of holiness to cleave to G-d (blessed be He), to Torah, and to the Tzaddikim, and to feel more deeply the greatness of G-d (blessed be He) and of Torah and of the Tzaddikim — each person according to what he measures in his own heart.

But those who establish themselves habitually with wine even on weekdays [yemei hachol] — and not only is all of this not sufficient for them, but through it they come to mockery [leitzanus] and controversy, and dispute with the truly righteous Tzaddikim — and even those people who are somewhat upright, who are not stirred by the drinking of wine toward outright mockery, but rather who err through it — for through the drinking he errs and misleads himself, until he inverts the truth and speaks perversely against those who truly fear G-d, because it seems to him that they have deviated from the truth, G-d forbid — and all of this error comes to him through excessive drinking of wine — regarding this it is said: "Whoever errs through it will not become wise". And their blemish and ruin through this is very great, as explained in the source text.

(Hilchos Yayin Nesech, Halacha 4, items 4, 7).

history.en: But there are Tzaddikim who are so great that they need no assistance from Above. And G-d conducts Himself with them as in the original thought — that is, through the attribute of strict judgment. And they stand firm through all the trials and sufferings and afflictions that derive from the attribute of judgment aforementioned. And they remain standing. And they sweeten the judgment at its very root — at the original thought. For they believe and know that the judgments and the sufferings themselves are great goodnesses. And through this they truly merit to ascend and be encompassed in the original thought — which is the aspect of: "Thus arose in thought" [kach alah b'machshavah] — said regarding the death of Rabbi Akiva. And this is the aspect of the tefillin of Rabbainu Tam — which are the aspect of the highest expanded consciousness [moichin govohim biyas]. And there the strengths precede the kindnesses. Which is the aspect of the governance that arose in the original thought — the aspect of the governance of the high Tzaddikim aforementioned.

segments.he:
י.
עקר אכילה דקדושה הוא כפי תקון הברית, כי צדיק אוכל לשבע נפשו, וצדיק הוא מאן דנטר ברית קדישא, כידוע. (הלכות מילה, הלכה ב', אות ט):
segments.en:
The essential eating in holiness is commensurate with the repair of the bris. For: "A Tzadik eats to the satisfaction of his soul" — and a Tzadik is defined as one who guards the holy bris [man d'natur bris kadisha], as is known.

(Hilchos Milah, Halacha 2, item 9).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And therefore one who wishes to draw close to G-d — to draw upon himself additional holiness — must also lay the tefillin of Rabbainu Tam. For all the distancing from G-d derives from the yetzer hara — whose root is from the attribute of judgment — drawn from the beginning of the contraction of the vacated space. And therefore the essential additional holiness is drawn upon a person through the tefillin of Rabbainu Tam — which are drawn from the aspect of the Tzaddikim aforementioned who ascend to the root of the judgment and sweeten everything at their root. Through which the power is drawn upon all the distant ones — to shatter and nullify the yetzer hara that is drawn from there.

segments.he:
יא.
על ידי אכילה פגומה, בפרט על ידי אכילה של אסור, חס ושלום, על ידי זה נפגמה היראה מאד, ומתגברין יראות הנפולות, יראות חיצונות, שהם בחינת קלפת עמלק, ימח שמו. (הלכות בכור בהמה טהורה, הלכה ד', אות ו ז):
segments.en:
Through blemished eating — especially through eating that which is forbidden, G-d forbid — through this the yirah [fear of G-d] is greatly blemished, and the fallen fears [yiros hanefilos] grow stronger — outer fears — which are the aspect of the husk of Amalek, may his name be blotted out.

(Hilchos Bechor Beheimah Tehorah, Halacha 4, items 6–7).

history.en: Now — in the footsteps of the Mashiach, at the end of the exile — when the exile and the baal davar and the sitra achra intensify greatly — and the essential [intensification] is that heresy [apikorsus] has spread and is spreading greatly in the world — all of this intensification is the aspect of the birth-pangs [chevlei leida] — the birth-pangs of the Mashiach. For all of this derives from the root of the judgment of the aspect of the vacated space aforementioned. And therefore there is now no power to stand against them — except through the power of the very great Tzaddikim aforementioned: who can enter there — into the aspect of the vacated space — and sweeten the judgment at its very root. Through which the entire power of the yetzer hara of all who come into the world — drawn from there — is nullified. Therefore every person must be careful to lay the tefillin of Rabbainu Tam — which are drawn from the aspect of the high expanded consciousness of those Tzaddikim aforementioned. In order to receive power from them — to shatter the yetzer hara that has now greatly intensified — drawn from there.

history.en: Sometimes when a person rebukes himself or his fellow and begins to recall the evil deeds that were done — it is common for him to fall even more and more. For he falls greatly in his mind. And there are those who have fallen greatly through this. And all of this derives from the aspect of rebuke that is not as it should be — which weakens the power of the soul through arousing the foul odor of sins. For the essential rebuke must be in the aspect of tilting toward kindness [mateh k'lapei chesed]: to seek and to find in oneself — and likewise in one's fellow — at the very least some good points. And the rebuke should be in the manner of kindness — to strengthen oneself and one's fellow in G-d — and to trust in His immense compassion. For He has such kindness — that even all the evil deeds can be transformed into merits. Even if one has greatly multiplied transgression, G-d forbid. For "with G-d is kindness, and with Him is abundant redemption, etc." And the essential rebuke should be in a manner that one strengthens himself and his fellow to awaken toward G-d — and to begin to draw close to Him from now on. And not that through his rebuke he causes even more ruin — that the person falls even more, G-d forbid. And for such rebuke one can only merit through binding oneself to the Tzaddikim of the generation — who are the aspect of Moshe. Through whose rebuke [the rebuke of such Tzaddikim] they add and bestow a good fragrance upon the souls.

segments.he:
א.
כשרוצים לבוא לארץ ישראל, ששם עקר כלליות כל הקדושות, אזי מתגברים ומשתטחים המניעות והעכובים, הנמשכים מבגדים הצואים, שאי אפשר להכניעם כי אם בכח התורה והצדיקים, והעקר - בכח קברי הצדיקים, שכבר נסתלקו ובאו למנוחתם. ועל כן כשראה כלב, שמתגברים מאד עצת המרגלים שרוצים לפגם בקדושת ארץ ישראל - הלך ונשתטח על קברי אבות, ועל כן גם בתחלת גאולת מצרים, שהיתה בשביל לבוא לארץ ישראל, כתיב: ויקח משה את עצמות יוסף עמו, בחינת קבר הצדיק. (הלכות בציעת הפת, הלכה ה', אות מז):
segments.en:
When one wishes to come to the Land of Israel — where the encompassing totality of all the holinesses resides — then the obstacles and hindrances intensify and spread, drawn from the begodim tzo'im [soiled garments], which cannot be subdued except through the power of Torah and the Tzaddikim, and primarily — through the power of the graves of the Tzaddikim who have already departed and come to their rest.

And therefore when Caleb saw that the counsel of the spies was growing very strong — seeking to blemish the holiness of the Land of Israel — he went and prostrated himself upon the graves of the Fathers. And likewise at the beginning of the redemption from Egypt, which was for the purpose of coming to the Land of Israel, it is written: "And Moshe took the bones of Yosef with him" — corresponding to the grave of the Tzadik.

(Hilchos Betziyas HaPas, Halacha 5, item 47).

history.en: The essential obligation to speak with one's fellow in fear of Heaven — and to illuminate within him the true divine knowledge — is only for the sake of broadening one's fellow's mind. For the essential [goal] is to bring out oneself and one's fellow from the aspect of moichin d'katnus [smallness of mind] to the aspect of moichin d'gadlus [greatness of mind]. That is, to strive that the mind should grow and expand more and more every single time. Which is the aspect of the broadening of the boundary of the Land of Israel — the aspect of: "And I will enlarge your boundary" [Exodus 34:24]. And therefore each person who engages in this — to speak with his fellow about the true holy knowledge — must every single time be careful to make a boundary [seyag] for his words and to be silent where one must be silent. So as not to demolish one's fellow's boundary entirely. For this is the aspect of the prohibition of encroachment [hasogos gevul]. For not only does he not strive to broaden his fellow's boundary — but he also oppresses him more and enters into his boundary. For every single person of Israel has a boundary for himself in his own mind — to attain and understand up to that very boundary — in the aspect of: "And you shall ascend — you and Aharon, etc." [Exodus 19:24] — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: "you to your half and Aharon to his half, etc."

segments.he:
ב.
עקר קדושת ארץ ישראל הוא על ידי התגלות הרצון, שמאיר שם, הינו להאמין שהכל מתנהג רק ברצונו יתברך ובהשגחתו לבד, וזה בחינת: כי רצו עבדיך את אבניה, כי הם בבחינת התגלות הרצון. (הלכות כלי היין, הלכה א', אות ו):
segments.en:
The essential holiness of the Land of Israel is through the revelation of ratzon [the Divine will] that shines there — that is, to believe that everything is guided solely by His blessed will and His Providence alone. And this is the aspect of: "For Your servants desired her stones" — for they are in the aspect of the revelation of the ratzon.

(Hilchos K'lai HaYayin, Halacha 1, item 6).

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And therefore even though certainly it is a great commandment to speak with one's fellow every single time in fear of Heaven — and to have compassion upon him and to bring him out from his sins and corruptions — even so, one must be very careful that the engagement be for the good and not for harm — to repair and not to cause more ruin, G-d forbid. Not to look too much at one's fellow's disgrace and his deficiencies. For most of the quarrels and disputes and causeless hatred derive only from this: that each person looks at his fellow not with a favorable eye — and seeks to find in him only the blemishes and evil character traits — until it seems to him that it is impossible to bear them. And naturally likewise his fellow also looks at him in the same reverse manner — for "as water reflects the face, etc." [Proverbs 27:19]. Until causeless hatred and quarrels are stirred between them. Until through this our Temple was destroyed — [was destroyed] — and the exile was prolonged over us. And all of it only on account of — [on account of] — causeless hatred. As our Sages of blessed memory said. And all of this comes only from looking too much at one's fellow.

segments.he:
ג.
עקר קדושת האמונה והחכמה דקדושה, שהם עקר החיים ואריכת ימים דקדושה, הוא בארץ ישראל, בחינת: למען ירבו ימיכם וגו', על האדמה. ובחוץ לארץ אין שום חיות כלל, רק על ידי מה שמשכימין ומעריבין בבתי כנסיוץ ומדרשות, ומתפללין ולומדין וקורין קריאת שמע, על ידי זה ממשיכין קדושת ארץ ישראל גם בחוץ לארץ, כי הם בחינת מקדש מעט, כמו שאמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה, וזה עקר חיותנו בזמן הגלות. (הלכות ספר תורה, הלכה ד', אות יז):
segments.en:
The essential holiness of faith and of holy wisdom — which are the very essence of life and the sacred length of days — is in the Land of Israel, in the aspect of: "So that your days may be many, etc., upon the land". And in the diaspora [chutz la'oretz] there is no vitality whatsoever — only through what one does by rising early and staying late in the synagogues and houses of study, and praying and learning and reciting the Kriyas Shma — through this one draws the holiness of the Land of Israel into the diaspora as well. For these are in the aspect of a mikdash me'at [miniature sanctuary], as our Sages of blessed memory said — and this is the very essence of our vitality during the time of exile.

(Hilchos Sefer Torah, Halacha 4, item 17).

history.en: For in truth one must judge every person to the scale of merit. For even though certainly one must speak with him and illuminate his mind and bring him out from what he needs to be brought out from — and all of this is the aspect of judgment and law [din u'mishpot] — as explained in the inner teachings — even so, one must overpower oneself with compassion to enter with one's fellow beyond the letter of the law [lifnim mishuras hadin]. Not to look at him for bad — only for good — [for good] — and to judge him to the scale of merit always. So that one can speak with him. And as is explained elsewhere — that this is the aspect of the commandment: "And you shall do what is right and good" [Deuteronomy 6:18]. From which our Sages of blessed memory derived [the obligation] to go beyond the letter of the law. And they also derived from this the law of bar metzra [the neighbor's right of first refusal] — which is the aspect of the commandment to strive to broaden one's fellow's boundary. And both are one.

segments.he:
ד.
ירושלים היא בחינת יראה שלמה ובושה ושפלות אמתי, שעל ידי זה עקר תקון האכילה דקדושה. (הלכות ערלה, הלכה ב', אות ד):
segments.en:
Jerusalem is the aspect of complete yirah [fear], and shame, and true humility — through which is the essential repair of holy eating.

(Hilchos Orlah, Halacha 2, item 4).

history.en: One who is on the lowest level — he must specifically find merit in himself — so as not to fall entirely, G-d forbid. And the essential purification and repentance of such a person is specifically through this. And this is the aspect of the purification of the parah adumah [the red heifer].

segments.he:
ה.
אף על פי שאנו מתחננים כל כך שנים הרבה לשוב לארץ ישראל ועדין אנו רחוקים משם, אוף על פי כן אין שום תפלה וצעקה נאבדת, אפלו של הפחות שבפחותים, כי בכל צעקה ותפלה כובשין איזה חלק ונקודה מארץ ישראל, עד שיתקבצו כל הנקודות שכבשנו בתפלותינו, ואז נשוב לארצנו בקרוב. ואפלו מי שהוא פגום מאד, ואין לו כח בצעקתו ותפלתו לכבש איזה נקודה וחלק מארץ ישראל, אוף על פי כן צעקתו פועל הרבה, כי הוא בחינת מחאה, המבאר בדין חזקת קרקעות, שכל זמן שהוא מוחה, אז אין חזקת המחזיק מועלת כלום, על כן אף על פי שהם גזלו מאתנו ארץ ישראל, שהיא ארצנו ונחלתנו, ואין בנו כח להוציאה מאתם מחמת פגם מעשינו, אוף על פי כן אנו מתפללים וצועקים בכל פעם, שארץ ישראל היא שלנו, כי היא נחלתנו, ובזה אנו עושין מחאה להסטרא אחרא, שידעו שאין חזקתם[חזקה כלל, כי ארץ ישראל היא שלנו מאבותינו, וסוף כל סוף נוציא אותה מידם, בעזרת השם. (הלכות חזקת מטלטלין, הלכה ה', אות יב):
segments.en:
Even though we have been supplicating for so many years to return to the Land of Israel and we are still far from there — even so, not a single prayer or cry is ever lost, even of the least of the least. For with each and every cry and prayer, some portion and point of the Land of Israel is conquered — until all the points we have conquered through our prayers will gather together, and then we will return to our land soon.

And even one who is very blemished and has no power in his cry and prayer to conquer any point or portion of the Land of Israel — even so, his cry accomplishes a great deal. For he is in the aspect of a mecho'ah [formal protest] — as is explained in the laws of chazakah [presumption of ownership of land]: that as long as one protests, the presumption of the one holding [the land] is of no effect whatsoever. Therefore, even though they have seized the Land of Israel from us — which is our land and our inheritance — and we do not have the power to extract it from them on account of the blemish of our deeds, even so, we pray and cry out every single time that the Land of Israel is ours, for it is our inheritance. And through this we make a mecho'ah [formal protest] against the sitra achra [the other side], so that they know that their presumption [chazakah] is no [presumption] at all — for the Land of Israel is ours from our forefathers, and in the end we will take it from their hands, with G-d's help.

(Hilchos Chazakas Metaltelin, Halacha 5, item 12).

history.en: The essential teshuvah is to return from pride — from which come all the sins, G-d forbid. And to humble oneself and feel one's lowliness and insignificance in truth. For the essential teshuvah is the submission and the lowliness and a broken heart before G-d. Through this He forgives him for all the sins — and all the judgments are nullified from him.

segments.he:
ו.
הזכרת שמות הצדיקים הוא דבר נפלא ונורא מאד מאד ומועיל הרבה מאד לעבודת השם יתברך, כמבאר במקום אחר. גם מסוגל לזכות על ידי זה לארץ ישראל, כי אי אפשר לבוא לארץ ישראל כי אם בכח הצדיקים אמתיים בבחינת: צדיקים יירשו ארץ וכו'. עין פנים ו"ימי נתן" בנסיעתו לארץ ישראל. (ועין לקוטי הלכות, הלכות נטילת ידים לסעודה, הלכה ד', אות ו, ובהלכות דברים הנוגעים בסעודה, הלכה ד', אות ו - ותבין יותר):
segments.en:
The mention of the names of the Tzaddikim is a wondrous and exceedingly — [exceedingly] — awesome thing, and is of very great benefit for the service of G-d (blessed be He), as is explained elsewhere. It is also a segula [-propitious means] to merit through this the Land of Israel — for it is impossible to come to the Land of Israel except through the power of the truly righteous Tzaddikim, in the aspect of: "The righteous shall inherit the land, etc.". See the source text and Yemei Nassan [the account of his journey] regarding his journey to the Land of Israel.

[See also Likutay Halachoas, Hilchos Netilas Yodayim L'seudah, Halacha 4, item 6, and Hilchos Devorim HaNoge'im B'seudah, Halacha 4, item 6 — and you will understand further.]

history.en: Our Sages of blessed memory said that for the severe sin of wasting seed, G-d protect us — teshuvah is not effective for it. And in truth this is fitting for it — as explained in the inner teachings. But in truth even so — there is nothing that stands before teshuvah. Only the essential repair is through the Tzadik of the generation — as is explained in the inner teachings.
